symbols.role: largest cumulant order admitted by the experiment

symbols.role: confounding magnitude in the explicit no-breakout witness

symbols.role: variance of the invariant Gaussian treatment source

symbols.name: \sigma_y^2
symbols.role: variance of the invariant Gaussian outcome source

symbols.role: compound-Poisson intensities in the no-breakout witness

symbols.name: N_{e,j}
symbols.role: Poisson counts in the no-breakout witness

novel.justification: This proposal-specific indexing restriction declares a positive latent-profile dimension; it is an uncited maintained restriction, not a literature contribution.
The count \(E\ge d+1\) is the model-specific minimum needed to house a rank-\(d\) calibration plane; it is an uncited design restriction, not a claimed literature contribution.
The finite order cap is a proposal-specific scope restriction fixing which cumulants and source moments are controlled; it is not attributed to prior work or claimed as a contribution.

assumptions.condition: \(\mathbb E[\epsilon_{u,e}]=\mathbb E[\epsilon_{t,e}]=\mathbb E[\epsilon_y]=0\) for every \(e\in\mathcal E\).
\(\epsilon_{u,e}\), \(\epsilon_{t,e}\), and \(\epsilon_y\) are mutually independent within every \(e\in\mathcal E\).
The moment generating function of each \(\epsilon_{u,e}\), \(\epsilon_{t,e}\), and \(\epsilon_y\) is finite for every real argument.

novel.justification: Global finiteness of the moment generating functions is a newly maintained model restriction satisfied by Gaussian and bounded-jump compound-Poisson sources.  Kivva et al. impose only a weaker local analytic-mgf antecedent.
The compact effect range is an uncited proposal-specific restriction used to state bounded loss and interval length; it is not a claimed literature contribution.

The loading bounds are uncited model-specific restrictions that exclude a degenerate treatment equation while allowing an open neighborhood around the explicit loading \(\alpha=1\); they are not claimed as a literature contribution.

The two-sided confounding bound is an uncited model-specific restriction ensuring that source swapping changes the causal effect by a material amount; it holds on ordinary compact coefficient neighborhoods and is not claimed as a contribution.

This source-level envelope is a newly maintained restriction satisfied by Gaussian and bounded-jump compound-Poisson families with intensities in compact sets.  Andrews and Guggenberger concern inference from supplied moments and are not support for this primitive source condition.

Full rank of the cumulant calibration matrix is an uncited proposal-specific relevance restriction.  It is directly satisfied by the scaled Vandermonde construction and is distinct from BACKSHIFT's joint-diagonalization condition.

The fixed calibration gap is an uncited model-specific stability restriction.  It holds for the explicit scaled Vandermonde family when \(\eta\sigma_d(V_d)\ge\kappa_0+\rho\), and is not attributed to BACKSHIFT.

This is a low-rank restriction on how one latent source changes across environments, not a restriction on a named estimator.  It is satisfied when environments modify the latent source through \(d\) shared intensity or mixture-weight factors, including finite compound-Poisson families with environment-dependent rates in a fixed \(d\)-dimensional span.

definitions.name: first projected breakout
definitions.construction: Set \(r^\star=\min\{k\ge d+2:Q_Ac_k\ne0\}\), with \(r^\star=\infty\) when every such flag vanishes.

definitions.name: bounded calibrated simultaneous-shift model
definitions.construction: \(\Theta=\{\theta=(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\{\epsilon_{u,e},\epsilon_{t,e}\}_{e\in\mathcal E},\epsilon_y): U_e=\epsilon_{u,e},\ T_e=\alpha U_e+\epsilon_{t,e},\ Y_e=\beta T_e+\gamma U_e+\epsilon_y,\ \theta\text{ satisfies every member property listed below}\}\).

definitions.name: swap-safe interior
definitions.construction: \(\Theta_\rho^\circ=\{\theta\in\Theta:\lvert\beta\rvert\le B-\rho,\ a_0+\rho\le\lvert\alpha\rvert\le a_1-\rho,\ q_0+\rho\le\lvert\gamma/\alpha\rvert\le q_1-\rho,\ \max_{e\in\mathcal E}\max_{X\in\{\epsilon_{u,e},\epsilon_{t,e},\epsilon_y\}}\mathbb E\lvert X\rvert^{2R_{\max}+\delta}\le M-\rho,\ \sigma_d(C)\ge\kappa_0+\rho\}\).

definitions.name: explicit Poisson--Gaussian no-breakout witness
definitions.construction: Fix \(E\ge d+1\) and positive \(q,L,\eta,\sigma_t^2,\sigma_y^2\) such that \(a_0+\rho\le1\le a_1-\rho\), \(q_0+\rho\le q\le q_1-\rho\), and \(q/2\le B-\rho\).  Let \(\lambda_{0,j}=L\) and \(\lambda_{e,j}=L+\eta\mathbf 1\{e=j\}\) for \(j=1,\ldots,d\), with all environments \(e>d\) at the baseline intensities, and take independent \(N_{e,j}\sim\operatorname{Poisson}(\lambda_{e,j})\).  Set \(\epsilon_{u,e}=\sum_{j=1}^d j(N_{e,j}-\lambda_{e,j})\), let every \(\epsilon_{t,e}\) have the common law \(\mathcal N(0,\sigma_t^2)\), take \(\epsilon_y\sim\mathcal N(0,\sigma_y^2)\), and make these sources mutually independent.  Set \(\alpha=1\), \(\beta=-q/2\), and \(\gamma=q\).  Require \(\eta\sigma_d(V_d)\ge\kappa_0+\rho\) and \[\max\left\{\max_{e\in\mathcal E}\mathbb E\left|\sum_{j=1}^d j(N_{e,j}-\lambda_{e,j})\right|^{2R_{\max}+\delta},\ \mathbb E|\epsilon_{t,0}|^{2R_{\max}+\delta},\ \mathbb E|\epsilon_y|^{2R_{\max}+\delta}\right\}\le M-\rho.\]

definitions.name: local first-breakout shell
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M_r(\lambda_n)=\{\theta\in\mathcal B:r^\star=r,\ \lambda_n\le\lVert Q_Ac_r\rVert_2\le2\lambda_n\}\) for each \(r\in\{d+2,\ldots,R_{\max}\}\) and sample size \(n\).

definitions.name: delayed-order compound-Poisson handle
definitions.construction: For a prescribed \(r\), start from strictly positive compound-Poisson jump intensities on \(\{1,\ldots,r\}\) and perturb the spare environment by signed intensity changes \(\varepsilon(-1)^{r-j}{r\choose j}\) at jump \(j\), with \(\varepsilon\) smaller than the baseline intensity margin; combine this with the exact source swap \(S\).

definitions.name: cumulant-SVD quotient GMM
definitions.construction: Construct \(\widehat c_k\) and \(\widehat m_k\) from symmetrized unbiased cumulant U-statistics, set \(\widehat C=[\widehat c_2\mid\cdots\mid\widehat c_{d+1}]\), let \(\widehat Q\) be the orthogonal complement projector from the rank-\(d\) SVD of \(\widehat C\), and set \(\widehat\beta\in\arg\min_{b\in[-B,B]}\max_{d+2\le k\le R_{\max}}\lVert\widehat Q(\widehat m_k-b\widehat c_k)\rVert_2\).

definitions.name: singularity-safe Anderson--Rubin inversion
definitions.construction: For a fixed deterministic calibration constant \(t_{\alpha_0}\), set \(\mathcal C_n=\{b\in[-B,B]:\max_{d+2\le k\le R_{\max}}\lVert\widehat Q(\widehat m_k-b\widehat c_k)\rVert_2\le t_{\alpha_0}/\sqrt n\}\), using \([-B,B]\) if the displayed set is empty or an environment has fewer than \(R_{\max}\) observations.

definitions.name: generated-projector influence handle
definitions.construction: Begin with the joint Hoeffding projections of the symmetrized cumulant U-statistics, apply the Fréchet derivative of the rank-\(d\) spectral projector at \(C\), and use a triangular-array Gaussian approximation formulated on the image of the possibly singular influence covariance.

statements.statement: For every \(\theta\in\Theta\) and integer \(k\ge2\), \(m_k-\beta c_k=\alpha^{k-1}\gamma u_k\in A\), and therefore \(Q_Am_k=\beta Q_Ac_k\).
statements.justification: Multilinearity and independent-source cancellation isolate the observable flag equation.
statements.gap: Kivva et al. derive scalar higher-moment ratios for one changing component; the vector projection that removes a jointly varying latent profile is new.
statements.consumer: The lemma supplies the estimable moment restriction used by the identification functional and every subsequent inference procedure.

statements.statement: Suppose \(E\ge d+1\) and positive \(q,L,\eta,\sigma_t^2,\sigma_y^2\) satisfy \(a_0+\rho\le1\le a_1-\rho\), \(q_0+\rho\le q\le q_1-\rho\), \(q/2\le B-\rho\), \(\eta\sigma_d(V_d)\ge\kappa_0+\rho\), and the \(2R_{\max}+\delta\)-moment maximum displayed in the explicit Poisson--Gaussian witness is at most \(M-\rho\).  For the resulting \(\theta\), every \(k\ge2\) obeys \(u_k=\eta(1^k,\ldots,d^k,0,\ldots,0)^\top\) and \(c_k=u_k\).  The leading \(d\times d\) block of \(C\) is \(\eta V_d=\eta[j^k]_{j=1,\ldots,d;\ k=2,\ldots,d+1}\), which is nonsingular because it is a Vandermonde matrix after factoring \(j^2\) from row \(j\); moreover \(\sigma_d(C)\ge\eta\sigma_d(V_d)\ge\kappa_0+\rho\).  Consequently \(A=\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf e_1,\ldots,\mathbf e_d\}\), every \(c_k\) lies in \(A\), and \(r^\star(\theta)=\infty\).  Under \(S\), the invariant Gaussian treatment source is the latent source, so every latent cumulant-shift vector is zero, while the observed \(C\) is unchanged and \(r^\star(S\theta)=\infty\).  In both representations, \(T_e=\epsilon_{u,e}+\epsilon_{t,e}\) and \(Y_e=(q/2)\epsilon_{u,e}-(q/2)\epsilon_{t,e}+\epsilon_y\), whereas the effects are respectively \(-q/2\) and \(q/2\).  Thus \(\theta,S\theta\in\Theta_\rho^\circ\), they generate the same \(P_e\) in every environment, \(\theta\in\mathcal N_\rho\), and \(\mathcal N_\rho\ne\varnothing\) for every compatible collection of bounds satisfying these feasibility conditions.
statements.justification: The explicit scaled-Vandermonde construction proves that the source-swap branch contains interior unequal-effect laws whenever the fixed bounds are jointly feasible.
statements.gap: Kivva et al.'s two-environment swap supplies the algebraic ambiguity, but it does not establish nonvacuity of this calibrated \(d\)-plane, fixed-gap, bounded-moment interior domain.
statements.consumer: The proposition ensures that the no-breakout verdict used for a Sachs edge corresponds to an attainable simultaneous-shift model rather than a branch created only by set notation.

statements.statement: Relative to \(\mathcal D_\rho\), \(\beta\) is identified at every \(\theta\in\mathcal B\) and, for every \(k\) with \(Q_Ac_k\ne0\), equals \(\langle Q_Ac_k,Q_Am_k\rangle/\lVert Q_Ac_k\rVert_2^2\).  At every \(\theta\in\mathcal N_\rho\), \(\theta\) and \(S\theta\) induce the same collection \(\{P_e:e\in\mathcal E\}\), both belong to \(\mathcal D_\rho\), and have distinct effects \(\beta\) and \(\beta+\gamma/\alpha\).  Hence \(\beta\) is identified in \(\mathcal D_\rho\) if and only if \(r^\star<\infty\).  The finite-breakout clause answers the multi-environment case isolated after Kivva et al., Theorem 3.6: every pairwise two-environment analysis may retain the source ambiguity while the joint law of \(E\ge d+2\) environments identifies \(\beta\) under the stated profile restriction.
statements.justification: This is the theorem-level kernel: the first environmental cumulant flag exactly separates the identified and source-label-ambiguous regions.
statements.gap: Kivva et al., Theorem 3.6, prove two-environment nonidentification under simultaneous source shifts and leave joint multi-environment rescue open; no published result supplies this iff projected-plane frontier.
statements.consumer: For a selected edge in the Sachs perturbation panel, the theorem either returns a direct-effect functional under the maintained profile restriction or records an exact structural ambiguity rather than a spurious estimate.

statements.statement: Under \(\operatorname{rank}(C)=d\), a finite breakout can occur only if \(E\ge d+2\).  If \(E=d+1\), then \(A=\mathbb R^d\) and \(Q_A=0\).  Conversely, for every \(d\ge1\), \(E\ge d+2\), and \(R_{\max}\ge d+2\), there exist finite \(M\), positive \(\kappa_0\), and one fixed choice of the remaining bounds such that, for every \(r\in\{d+2,\ldots,R_{\max}\}\), centered independent entire-mgf source laws satisfy those same bounds and calibration gap with \(r^\star=r\).
statements.justification: The environment count is an exact resource threshold once the latent profile dimension is fixed.
statements.gap: BACKSHIFT's three-setting threshold concerns covariance joint diagonalization; the proposed \(d+2\) threshold concerns a selected confounded effect and includes realizability at every prescribed higher order.
statements.consumer: The result tells experimentalists how many perturbation environments are minimally required to leave a \(d\)-factor latent-shift geometry.

statements.statement: For every \(r\in\{d+2,\ldots,R_{\max}\}\), there is a nondegenerate finite-dimensional Poisson--Gaussian subclass of \(\mathcal B\) containing \(\theta_0\) and \(\theta_1\) with \(\beta(\theta_0)\ne\beta(\theta_1)\), \(r^\star(\theta_0)=r^\star(\theta_1)=r\), and \(\mathbb E_{\theta_0}[T_e^pY_e^{\ell}]=\mathbb E_{\theta_1}[T_e^pY_e^{\ell}]\) for every \(e\in\mathcal E\) and every \(p,\ell\ge0\) with \(p+\ell<r\).
statements.justification: The first breakout order is information-theoretically meaningful, not an artifact of one estimator's search loop.
statements.gap: Existing cumulant methods assume a useful nonzero order; they do not construct legal unequal-effect SEMs that match every lower observed mixed moment and become identified exactly at the prescribed order.
statements.consumer: The theorem prevents analysts from truncating the moment search below \(r\) while claiming uniform identification over delayed-breakout environments.

statements.statement: In the special case \(d=1\) and \(E=2\), \(\operatorname{rank}(C)=1\) implies \(A=\mathbb R\) and \(Q_A=0\), so the finite-breakout branch is empty and the legal source-swap pair reproduces the already-known simultaneous-noise nonidentification of Kivva et al., Theorem 3.6.
statements.justification: This reduction checks that the new frontier collapses to the closest known result at the two-environment boundary.
statements.gap: This is already known from Kivva et al., Theorem 3.6, and is included only as a fidelity reduction rather than a novelty claim.
statements.consumer: It lets users interpret the new condition as a strict joint-environment rescue of the established two-environment obstruction.

statements.statement: For each fixed \(r\in\{d+2,\ldots,R_{\max}\}\) and every nonempty shell \(\mathcal M_r(\lambda_n)\), the minimax squared error for estimating \(\beta\) is of order \(\min\{B^2,(n\lambda_n^2)^{-1}\}\), and the minimax worst-case expected length among intervals with coverage at least \(1-\alpha_0\) uniformly on \(\mathcal D_\rho\) is of order \(\min\{B,(\sqrt n\lambda_n)^{-1}\}\).  The estimator \(\widehat\beta\) and interval \(\mathcal C_n\) attain the respective upper bounds without knowing \(r\); uniform consistency on a shell sequence holds if and only if \(\sqrt n\lambda_n\to\infty\).
statements.justification: The theorem quantifies how quickly the exact identifying flag may approach the nonidentified boundary before estimation and honest inference fail.
statements.gap: Causal Dantzig and environmental GMM give regular inference, while Andrews and Guggenberger give generic singularity-robust testing for supplied moments; none derives this structural rate frontier with an estimated cumulant plane and a full-observation causal lower-bound family.  The conversion of the testing rate into honest-interval length is an incremental standard consequence rather than a separate novelty claim.
statements.consumer: The rate converts an empirical flag magnitude in protein-signaling environments into a principled precision and consistency diagnostic.

statements.statement: For every \(\theta\in\mathcal N_\rho\), any random interval with coverage at least \(1-\alpha_0\) at both \(\theta\) and \(S\theta\) satisfies \(\mathbb E_\theta[\operatorname{length}(\mathcal C_n)]\ge(1-2\alpha_0)\lvert\gamma/\alpha\rvert\).
statements.justification: Exact observational equivalence forces a nonvanishing honest interval at the no-breakout boundary.
statements.gap: This honest-interval consequence is an incremental application of the standard two-point coverage argument; Kivva et al.'s population nonidentification result does not state the \(1-2\alpha_0\) expected-length factor.
statements.consumer: The proposition prevents a narrow reported interval from masking exact source-label ambiguity when every flag vanishes.

statements.statement: Can one establish, uniformly over triangular arrays in \(\mathcal M_r(\lambda_n)\) with \(\sqrt n\lambda_n\to\infty\), a first-order influence expansion and Gaussian approximation for the cumulant-SVD estimator that includes the same-sample estimated-\(A\) correction, remains valid when the influence covariance is singular, and yields asymptotically calibrated singularity-robust Anderson--Rubin inversion?
statements.justification: This is the principal open proof boundary between conservative rate-optimal inversion and a sharp limit law with calibrated critical values.
statements.gap: Long et al. treat regular environmental GMM, Andrews and Guggenberger treat supplied singular moments, and Davis--Kahan perturbation theory controls projector stability; none derives a uniform cumulant U-statistic expansion through a same-sample estimated spectral projector.
statements.consumer: A solution gives practitioners efficient calibrated confidence sets when the flag is weak and the projected moment covariance loses rank.

sampling_model.design: Independent stratified sampling from \(E\) fixed environments with deterministic counts \(n_e\).
sampling_model.units: Within each environment, \((T_{e,i},Y_{e,i})_{i=1}^{n_e}\) are independent draws from \(P_e\), and samples are independent across environments.
sampling_model.treatment: The treatment is generated by \(T_e=\alpha U_e+\epsilon_{t,e}\); there is no randomized assignment.
sampling_model.overlap: Not applicable; identification comes from environmental cumulant shifts rather than treatment propensity overlap.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Cumulants through \(R_{\max}\) are estimated by symmetrized U-statistics and \(A\) by the rank-\(d\) SVD of \(\widehat C\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 3.6 proves that \(\beta\) is not identifiable from two environments when both \(\epsilon_u\) and \(\epsilon_t\) change.
Theorem 1 gives uniqueness of the BACKSHIFT joint diagonalizer if and only if every pair of intervention-variance profiles is nonproportional across environments.
Theorem 3.1 makes Causal Dantzig invariance identical to GMM moments, and regular GMM theory yields asymptotic normality and optimal weighting.
The paper's SR-AR and SR-CQLR tests have uniformly correct asymptotic size without restrictions on identification strength or moment-covariance eigenvalues.
Causal Dantzig identifies a linear causal coefficient through an invertible covariance-difference moment and gives regular low-dimensional confidence intervals.
Under perfect interventions, one intervention on each latent node is sufficient and worst-case necessary for coupled-cumulant recovery of linear causal disentanglement parameters.
Higher-order cumulants identify latent-variable LiNGAM effects when a proxy or underspecified instruments provide auxiliary source information.
The paper characterizes bivariate effect identifiability by exogenous-noise Gaussianity without auxiliary variables.

tldr: Simultaneous changes in latent and treatment noises create an exact source-label ambiguity in two environments.  When the environment-indexed latent cumulant shifts occupy an unknown calibrated \(d\)-plane, the orthogonal treatment cumulant flag \(Q_Ac_k\) resolves that ambiguity exactly: its first nonzero order identifies \(\beta\) by a projected mixed-cumulant quotient, while global absence of a flag admits a legal unequal-effect source swap.  An explicit scaled-Vandermonde compound-Poisson construction places both unequal-effect representations in the bounded interior whenever the displayed coefficient, gap, and moment inequalities are feasible, so the no-breakout branch is nonempty rather than formal.  The environment threshold \(E=d+2\) and every possible first identifying order are sharp, and a companion weak-breakout theorem targets minimax risk while the same-sample projector expansion with singular covariance remains the principal open-ended question.

project_justification.gap: The closest higher-moment paper handles two environments and either one changing component or simultaneous-shift nonidentification.  It explicitly leaves open whether environments can identify an effect jointly when pairwise comparisons fail.  Covariance-based multi-environment methods use a different diagonal-shift geometry and cannot resolve the treatment-versus-latent source label in this model.
project_justification.niche: A low-rank restriction on latent environmental cumulant profiles creates a joint geometric signal that is invisible to every pairwise analysis.  The resulting first-breakout order is simultaneously an identification boundary, an environment-design resource, and a statistical strength parameter.
project_justification.fill: The project gives an if-and-only-if observed-law frontier, an explicit compatible-bounds construction proving that its no-breakout branch contains interior unequal-effect laws, a sharp \(d+2\) environment threshold, realizable lower-order-indistinguishable models at every cumulant order, and a rate-optimal inference program whose unresolved generated-projector limit theory is stated openly.

related_work: Kivva, Akbari, Salehkaleybar, and Kiyavash (2025), especially Theorem 3.6 and its source-swap proof, supply the closest obstruction and the mixed-cumulant algebra; their local analytic-mgf antecedent is weaker than the globally finite-mgf restriction maintained here.  The present target answers their stated multi-environment question under a new low-rank profile restriction and is positioned as informed by, rather than as a strict tightening of, that theorem.  Rothenhäusler, Heinze, Peters, and Meinshausen (2015) give BACKSHIFT's contrasting covariance joint-diagonalization condition; that paper does not support the present loading, calibration-rank, or calibration-gap restrictions.  Cai et al. (2023), Leyes Carreno, Meroni, and Seigal (2025), and Tramontano et al. (2025) demonstrate higher-cumulant recovery under one-latent-component, targeted-intervention, proxy, or instrumental structure; none supplies the environmental source-label frontier here.  Li, Kwok, Guo, and Liu (2026) characterize effect identifiability from one bivariate law according to noise Gaussianity and publicly exclude constrained multi-environment settings from scope; the complete proof text was externally inaccessible during this scan, so the paper is treated only as an informed-by comparator.  Long et al. (2023) provide the environmental GMM template in a regular supplied-moment model.  Andrews and Guggenberger (2019) provide singularity-robust Anderson--Rubin inference for high-level supplied moments and do not support the primitive source moment envelope.  Davis and Kahan (1970) are cited solely for stability of the estimated spectral projector under matrix perturbation.  Causal Dantzig supplies regular covariance-shift inference.  These results inform, but do not establish, the generated-projector weak-breakout theorem.  Mooij, Magliacane, and Claassen (2020) explain why unknown intervention targets, latent confounding, and feedback are material in the Sachs application, while Sachs et al. (2005) provide the multi-perturbation single-cell setting rather than evidence that the new latent-profile condition holds.
technical_internal_limitation: The load-bearing unresolved calculation is the uniform first-order expansion of projected cumulant U-statistics when \(A\) is estimated from the same samples.  The derivative of the projector contributes at first order, and the influence covariance can be exactly singular.  The early kill test is the case \(d=1\), \(E=3\), and \(r=3\): a covariance-preserving Gaussian--Hermite local family must remain positive and inside one fixed bounded model for \(\beta\in[1.9,2.3]\), have full-observation Kullback--Leibler divergence bounded by \(Cn\lambda_n^2(\beta-\beta')^2\), and reproduce the estimated-plane correction.  Failure of same-model legality or of this density-level bound kills the minimax spine but not the exact identification theorem.
honest_scope: The identification if-and-only-if is confined to the explicitly source-labelled union \(\mathcal D_\rho\), not arbitrary simultaneous shifts.  The explicit no-breakout construction proves nonemptiness only for fixed bounds admitting positive \(q,L,\eta,\sigma_t^2,\sigma_y^2\) that satisfy the displayed interior, singular-gap, and moment inequalities; incompatible bounds carry no nonemptiness claim.  The entire-mgf condition is newly maintained here as a strict global strengthening of the local analytic-mgf antecedent used by Kivva et al.  The \(d=1,E=2\) reduction is already known from Kivva et al., Theorem 3.6, and the no-breakout honest-length proposition is an incremental standard consequence.  A failed finite scan through \(R_{\max}\) does not establish global no-breakout outside this domain.  The Sachs data motivate the consumer but do not verify the structural restrictions.  The conservative Anderson--Rubin interval does not require a nonsingular covariance; asymptotically calibrated Gaussian inversion remains open in \(\text{oeq:generated-projector-limit}\).

seed_details.anchor_location: Introduction, Theorem 3.6 and its source-swap proof, and Conclusion
seed_details.question: Characterize identification of \(\beta\) when both latent and treatment noises shift but all latent cumulant-shift profiles lie in an unknown calibrated \(d\)-plane.
seed_details.changed_proof_step: Replace the two-environment scalar cumulant difference in Kivva et al. by the orthogonal projection of the environment-indexed cumulant vector off the calibrated latent plane; the necessity step must verify that the source swap remains inside the same bounded model.
seed_details.destination_search: A targeted search for multi-environment higher-order-moment effect identification under simultaneous latent- and treatment-noise changes returned Kivva et al. and adjacent cumulant papers, but no projected low-rank flag or identification-if-and-only-if result.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from Kivva et al. because their source-swap argument and cumulant ratios already apply pairwise in any number of environments.
seed_details.rebuttal: Pairwise use does not exploit a joint environment subspace; their Conclusion expressly separates cases identifiable jointly but not pairwise, and their paper contains neither the projected functional nor the legal all-environment converse.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The seed is not a sufficient-only ratio: it states both the breakout functional and a same-domain observational-equivalence converse over a uniform class.

seed_details.anchor_location: Introduction, Theorem 1 and Corollary 1, proof construction in the identifiability appendix, and Conclusion
seed_details.question: Is \(E=d+2\) the sharp environment threshold for a treatment-noise cumulant contrast to leave a calibrated \(d\)-plane?
seed_details.changed_proof_step: Replace BACKSHIFT's pairwise nonproportional diagonal variance profiles by the dimension of the orthogonal complement of the latent cumulant plane; sufficiency requires realizable noise laws, not arbitrary contrast vectors.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches pairing environment count with cumulant-plane effect identification found BACKSHIFT's covariance threshold and Kivva et al.'s two-environment analysis, but no \(d+2\) threshold indexed by latent profile rank.
seed_details.red_team: This is elementary dimension counting once \(A\) is defined.
seed_details.rebuttal: Necessity is dimension counting, but sharpness also demands legal entire-mgf SEMs with full calibration rank and a prescribed first breakout order; that realizability construction is not automatic.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The theorem is paired with explicit attainability and is not presented as a generic three-environment analogue of BACKSHIFT.

seed_details.anchor_location: Algorithms 1--4, the smallest-differing-order loops, Theorems 3.2--3.5 and their cumulant proofs, and Conclusion
seed_details.question: For every prescribed order \(r\), can two unequal-effect legal models agree in all observed mixed moments below \(r\) while both become identified at order \(r\)?
seed_details.changed_proof_step: Turn Kivva et al.'s search for the first nonzero moment into a necessity construction using positive compound-Poisson intensities whose signed rate perturbation is an \(r\)-th finite difference.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for causal moment-order lower bounds based on compound-Poisson finite differences found higher-cumulant identification papers but no realizable unequal-effect matched-order twins in the simultaneous-shift model.
seed_details.red_team: Moment matching is a standard finite-difference trick and says nothing about causal identification.
seed_details.rebuttal: The nontrivial step is to embed the signed perturbation as changes of strictly positive source intensities in two observationally equivalent unequal-effect SEMs while preserving calibration, first-breakout order, and all model bounds.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The result ranges over every \(r\le R_{\max}\) and a finite-dimensional neighborhood of legal intensities, not a single hand-tuned law.

seed_details.anchor_location: Population moment formulas, simulation estimators, and Conclusion
seed_details.question: Determine minimax risk and uniformly honest confidence length when the first projected cumulant flag has magnitude \(\lambda_n\).
seed_details.changed_proof_step: After the population cumulant quotient, differentiate through an estimated spectral projector and build a full-observation local family whose density, rather than only its moments, changes at order \(\lambda_n\lvert\beta-\beta'\rvert\).
seed_details.destination_search: Weak-GMM and singularity-robust searches found Andrews and Guggenberger, Poskitt, and Wang, Chan, and Ye, but none treats high-order cumulants with a same-sample estimated projector or supplies a causal same-shell full-law lower bound.
seed_details.red_team: The rate is the ordinary weak-instrument rate with the breakout merely renamed instrument strength.
seed_details.rebuttal: Generic weak-GMM begins with a supplied moment map; here the projector is generated from lower cumulants, the covariance may be singular, and the lower bound must be realized by full observed SEM laws in the same breakout shell.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: This is an M11 rate frontier with an explicit structural regime parameter and a full-data converse, not a bare estimation rung.

seed_details.anchor_location: Smallest-order loops in Algorithms 1--4 and Conclusion
seed_details.question: Can the first identifying cumulant order be selected while maintaining uniform effect coverage over delayed, local, and absent flags?
seed_details.changed_proof_step: Rewrite each order in the population search loop as a null moment in \(\beta\), then calibrate their joint maximum after accounting for the common estimated projector.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches combining post-selection cumulant order, causal effects, and estimated subspaces found generic Gaussian-maxima theory but no valid selection-and-inversion theorem for this target-method pair.
seed_details.red_team: Bonferroni or multiplier bootstrap makes the result immediate because \(R_{\max}\) is fixed.
seed_details.rebuttal: Simultaneous calibration is only one piece: the no-breakout intersection is singular, the moment coordinates share an estimated subspace, and honest adaptation cannot consistently distinguish exact zeros from local flags without an explicit separation or loss theorem.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The open object is an honest adaptive confidence procedure and its unavoidable loss, not consistent first-order selection asserted without separation.

seed_details.anchor_location: Population identifying formulas and empirical moment algorithms
seed_details.question: Derive the semiparametric efficiency bound for \(\beta\) on a fixed positive-breakout shell and characterize when projected cumulant GMM attains it.
seed_details.changed_proof_step: Replace the paper's plug-in moment ratios by a tangent-space calculation for environment-stratified laws subject to the cumulant-plane restriction.
seed_details.destination_search: Targeted searches found optimal environmental GMM weighting but no efficiency bound for the nonlinear law class with an estimated cumulant plane.
seed_details.red_team: Optimal GMM weighting from Long et al. already gives the efficiency statement.
seed_details.rebuttal: Optimality within a finite moment list is not the semiparametric efficiency bound over the full observed-law model, and the projector nuisance changes the tangent calculation.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: This is the underrepresented efficiency-bound lane, but it is not selected because the tangent space is less mature than the exact-identification kernel.

seed_details.anchor_location: Introduction, population joint-diagonalization objective, Theorem 1 and proof, and Conclusion
seed_details.question: Give a necessary-and-sufficient cumulant-rank condition for a selected equilibrium intervention response in a stable cyclic system with simultaneous latent and node-noise shifts.
seed_details.changed_proof_step: Replace BACKSHIFT's covariance congruence by higher-order cumulant tensors transported through the equilibrium resolvent, and replace its row-mixing necessity construction by a stability-preserving source swap.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches pairing stable cyclic equilibrium effects with higher-order environmental cumulants found BACKSHIFT, cyclic causal calculus, and non-Gaussian simultaneous-equation work, but no simultaneous-shift effect frontier.
seed_details.red_team: This is BACKSHIFT with cumulants substituted for covariances.
seed_details.rebuttal: Cyclic cumulants transform multilinearly rather than by matrix congruence, and the desired target is one equilibrium intervention response under simultaneous source changes, so both the recovery functional and the necessity construction change at the first proof step.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The seed does not default to acyclic effect algebra; it identifies a resolvent-based structural object and its indeterminacy.

seed_details.anchor_location: Exact moment equations, nonidentification theorem, and Conclusion
seed_details.question: Under a radius \(\delta\) for latent cumulant leakage outside \(A\), derive sharp bounds for \(\beta\) and the smallest \(\delta^\star\) at which a selected effect sign can reverse.
seed_details.changed_proof_step: Relax the projected equality \(Q_A(m_k-\beta c_k)=0\) into a source-derived residual set and compute the induced one-dimensional support function before applying bias-aware GMM inference.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches found approximate-moment confidence intervals and graphical robustness analyses of Sachs data, but no mapping from latent-source cumulant leakage to a sharp effect interval or critical radius.
seed_details.red_team: This is a direct scalar application of approximate GMM sensitivity.
seed_details.rebuttal: A valid leakage radius must first be mapped from primitive source deviations to the projected mixed-cumulant residual; without that sharp map the generic approximate-GMM interval is not the causal identified set.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The seed names closed endpoints and a critical \(\delta^\star\), avoiding sufficient-only sensitivity.

seed_details.anchor_location: Theorem 1, its necessity proof, intervention-variance reconstruction, and Conclusion
seed_details.question: Recover a multivariate linear mechanism up to source-label permutations by combining covariance and higher-cumulant environmental flags when several source profiles are collinear at order two.
seed_details.changed_proof_step: Replace exact joint diagonalization of covariance differences by a coupled decomposition across cumulant orders with an order-dependent label-separation certificate.
seed_details.destination_search: The destination search found coroICA and linear causal disentanglement via coupled cumulant tensors; those papers occupy substantial parts of the structure-recovery target.
seed_details.red_team: Coupled higher-order tensor decomposition already recovers this mechanism in Leyes Carreno, Meroni, and Seigal.
seed_details.rebuttal: The exact simultaneous-shift class differs, but the closest literature occupies too much of the recovery-map contribution to sustain a clean novelty claim.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: This M18 seed was rejected after the adjacent-thread scan rather than relabeled as effect identification.

threads.settled: Theorem 3.6 constructs the exact source swap and proves nonidentification when both source noises change in two environments; the Conclusion identifies joint use of more than two environments as future work.
threads.gap: No joint low-rank environment geometry, projected recovery functional, or iff boundary is given.

threads.settled: Theorem 1 gives an iff condition for joint covariance diagonalization in stable cyclic systems and Corollary 1 shows that at least three environments are required.
threads.gap: Its diagonal shift-covariance model neither permits the present simultaneous latent-source ambiguity nor identifies the selected confounded effect through higher cumulants.

threads.settled: Coupled higher-order cumulants recover latent causal disentanglement parameters under one targeted intervention per latent node, while soft interventions leave a positive-dimensional parameter class.
threads.gap: The intervention target structure is different and there is no treatment-effect quotient after projecting an unknown source-profile plane.

threads.settled: Higher cumulants identify latent-variable LiNGAM effects when a proxy or underspecified instruments label source roots.
threads.gap: The auxiliary-variable labels replace, rather than solve, simultaneous environmental source-label ambiguity.

threads.settled: The ICML paper characterizes effect identifiability from one treatment--outcome law according to exogenous-noise Gaussianity without auxiliary variables.
threads.gap: Its publicly indexed scope note excludes constrained multi-environment settings of the present kind; the browser challenge prevented fresh verification of the full theorem proof, so no load-bearing comparison is assigned to it.

threads.settled: The identifying algorithms search for a first nonzero moment difference under one changing component.
threads.gap: They do not prove that every candidate order is necessary through realizable unequal-effect models matching all lower mixed moments.

threads.settled: Higher cumulants and a one-latent-component condition recover mixing information and causal order in latent-variable LiNGAM.
threads.gap: No environment-indexed moment-order lower bound or causal source-swap twins are constructed.

threads.settled: A fixed nonzero higher-order cumulant tensor supports constructive coupled decomposition.
threads.gap: The paper does not characterize the first necessary order or construct laws indistinguishable through all lower orders.

threads.settled: Theorem 3.1 equates Causal Dantzig invariance with GMM moments, and the regular theory gives optimal weighting and asymptotic normality under a full-rank Jacobian.
threads.gap: The moment map is supplied and regular; it has no estimated spectral projector, high-order cumulants, weak denominator, or causal minimax converse.

threads.settled: Andrews and Guggenberger's SR-AR and SR-CQLR tests have uniform asymptotic size without identification or nonsingularity requirements for a supplied moment function.
threads.gap: The theorem does not derive a generated cumulant moment expansion or a structural full-law minimax rate.

threads.settled: Causal Dantzig gives low-dimensional regular intervals under additive interventions and a nonsingular population covariance contrast.
threads.gap: It notes instability under weak shifts but provides neither a local-strength frontier nor uniformly honest inference through zero.

threads.settled: Many-weak-moment GMM with nuisance parameters admits debiased inference under high-level orthogonality and rate conditions.
threads.gap: It does not verify those high-level conditions for a cumulant U-statistic projector or supply same-model density-level lower bounds.
